title: The Doomed - initial thoughts / solo narrative skirmish gaming / Into the Odd
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PkjXvpbR1q8

Daniel (@dungeondive) shares early thoughts on The Doomed: Apocalyptic Horror Hunting, the rules-light narrative skirmish game from Chris McDowall, creator of Into the Odd, and Osprey. He predicts it will do for skirmish games what Into the Odd did for indie RPGs. He's testing it on a single Loke battle-mat book with Star Saga miniatures. He says firmly that kitbashing and terrain-building are optional: the hobby's focus on modelling does it a disservice.

The whole system rests on one stat, quality (3+, 4+ or 5+), which is the number you roll for everything. There's no measuring and no hit points. Your first move is free, and when you're damaged you roll on a shock table that might hand you a last gasp, give an ally vengeance, or leave you slaughtered on snake eyes. Warbands are bought with renown, mostly fit on half a sheet of paper, and face one of five Dooms (hunger, hatred, domination, oblivion and ruin), each with its own event table.

Most of the 173 pages generate scenarios. You roll d66 for a Horror and d66 for a Conflict and mash them together, Monster Hunter-style. His live roll pairs a Techno Basilisk, which you weaken by destroying its three nexuses, with a maze of tunnels. Defeated Horrors drop parts you can use to arm your warband. His tip for 2D maps: dry-erase elevation numbers onto buildings. A full campaign is planned for 2024.

----

The Doomed runs on one stat and no measuring. How simple can a skirmish game get before it stops feeling like a skirmish game for you?
